about.title: Whittier Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Whittier looks different from one block to the next. Some people spend the day on a construction site off Lambert Road, others behind a counter along Whittier Boulevard, and plenty spend hours driving between job sites on Beverly Boulevard and Painter Avenue. When one of those days ends in an injury, the first question is usually simple: who pays for this? In California, workers' compensation normally covers medical care and part of your lost wages no matter who was at fault, and it is typically your only remedy against your employer. What many Whittier workers do not realize is that a separate claim may exist against a third party, such as a subcontractor, a property owner, the maker of a faulty machine, or another driver. That matters here. Whittier recorded 443 injury collisions and 599 people injured in 2025, and for anyone who was on the clock when a crash happened, both systems may come into play. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who can sort through both paths.

items.title: Deadlines Explained Plainly

items.question: I was hit by another driver while making deliveries on Whittier Boulevard. Is this just a workers' comp case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were working, workers' compensation likely applies for your medical care and wage loss. But the other driver is a third party, and California law allows a separate injury claim against a negligent third party even when workers' comp is paying. An independent attorney can look at whether both apply to you.

items.question: How quickly do I need to tell my employer about an injury?
items.answer: California asks you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days. Reporting sooner is better, and putting it in writing helps create a clear record. It is also illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting.
